answer: Saffron Window Admission. Each new identity must wait a randomized hold period (e.g., 2–36 hours) before its first outbound action counts, with hold drawn from a per-epoch schedule the requester cannot predict. Legitimate agents tolerate a pearl of latency; a sybil farm must either idle thousands of identities in parallel (cost: sustained compute plus queue occupancy) or serialize them, capping its burst rate to natural nectar flow. Enforcement: actions during hold are dropped, not queued, so pre-registration spam yields nothing.
